z-m-21-01.title: Conclusion “only one”: e really only one?
z-m-21-01.topic: Write degree-4 expression as product of two quadratics: check all cases
z-m-21-01.goal: Check claim “only one” made after seeing some cases; make different quadratic products for same quartic and explain why factorisation count remains fixed even with wider conditions. [4]
z-m-21-01.material: Jiho write x⁴−5x²+4 as (x²+ax+b)(x²+cx+d). Both quadratics have x² coefficient 1; a,b,c,d integers; swapping factors count same. Jiho say “only one factorisation.” (Read x⁴ fourth power, x² squared, ac a times c.)
z-m-21-01.thinking.0: Find line where case left out
z-m-21-01.thinking.2: Judge how conclusion change when condition change (integers to real numbers)
z-m-21-01.prereq.0: Expand product of quadratics and collect same-degree terms (Common Math polynomial unit level, Grade 9 to Grade 10) [3 1]
z-m-21-01.prereq.1: Meaning of two polynomials being same expression in x (identity). Activity grade only describes task difficulty, not curriculum placement.
z-m-21-01.prereq.2: Experience expanding products of linear expressions like (x−1)(x+1)
z-m-21-01.s.s1.prompt: Which line make Jiho “only one” conclusion hard to believe as written? Choose one.
z-m-21-01.s.s1.hint.0: Mark whether each line follow from previous one, and find first line where “this only one” appear.
z-m-21-01.s.s1.hint.1: For line with a list like “one of these,” such as line 4, remake list under same condition and compare item by item.
z-m-21-01.s.s1.line.0: Expand (x²+ax+b)(x²+cx+d), match each degree coefficient to x⁴−5x²+4.
z-m-21-01.s.s1.line.1: x³ coefficient give a+c=0 so c=−a; x coefficient ad+bc=a(d−b)=0, so a=0 or b=d.
z-m-21-01.s.s1.line.3: b,d integers with product 4, so pairs (1,4),(4,1),(2,2). [1 1 2 2 4 4]
z-m-21-01.s.s1.line.4: Only pair meeting x² coefficient b+d−a²=−5 na b=d=2,a=3 (or a=−3).
z-m-21-01.s.s1.explain: Lines 1–3 calculations correct (x² coefficient b+d+ac; c=−a makes b+d−a²). Line 4 first error: integer factor pairs also (−1,−4),(−4,−1),(−2,−2); only positive ones listed. Line 5 correct only within that incomplete list, so line 6 “only one” unsupported. Even if choose line 6, issue no be its calculation but whether earlier checked all cases. [1 3 4 4 1 4 4 1 2 2 5 6 6]
z-m-21-01.s.s2.prompt: Make 2 different (x²+ax+b)(x²+cx+d) factorizations equal x⁴−5x²+4. Integers a,b,c,d; order-only differences same. [5 4]
z-m-21-01.s.s2.hint.0: Remake list of b,d values from Jiho solution and also test unlisted pairs in remaining coefficient conditions.
z-m-21-01.s.s2.hint.1: Split into a=0 case and b=d case, then find b,d in each.
z-m-21-01.s.s2.fail.c1: After expansion, x³ coefficient a+c no be 0.
z-m-21-01.s.s2.fail.c2: After expansion, x² coefficient b+d+ac no be −5.
z-m-21-01.s.s2.fail.c3: After expansion x coefficient ad+bc no be 0.
z-m-21-01.s.s2.fail.c4: After expansion constant bd no be 4.
z-m-21-01.s.s2.explain: Three integer factorisations possible: (x²−1)(x²−4), (x²+3x+2)(x²−3x+2), (x²+x−2)(x²−x−2). Jiho found only one. Order-swapped forms like a and −a count same.
z-m-21-01.s.s2.because.prompt: If two different groupings both give x⁴−5x²+4, where Jiho “only one” go wrong? Write 2–3 sentences and use one expression you made. [5 4]
z-m-21-01.s.s2.because.hint.0: Expand both groupings you made and check if results same expression.
z-m-21-01.s.s2.because.hint.1: Compare Jiho way of arranging cases with your groupings: dey they on his list?
z-m-21-01.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: Did you expand to verify expression really equal x⁴−5x²+4?
z-m-21-01.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: Did you identify mistake as “left out possible cases” rather than calculation error?
z-m-21-01.s.s2.because.selfAssess.2: Did you say wetin needed before claiming “only one”?
z-m-21-01.s.s2.because.model.0: Expanding (x²−1)(x²−4) give x⁴−5x²+4; expanding (x²+3x+2)(x²−3x+2) give same. Both correct, so no be only one. Jiho omit negative pairs with product 4, leaving only one.
z-m-21-01.s.s2.because.modelNote.0: Mention counterexample (another grouping) and cause (cases left out).
z-m-21-01.s.s2.because.model.1: x⁴−5x²+4=(x−1)(x+1)(x−2)(x+2). Grouping four linear factors into pairs fit give many quadratic products, like (x²+x−2)(x²−x−2). Jiho conclude one because e find only one way without checking every case.
z-m-21-01.s.s2.because.modelNote.1: Explain from another view: grouping linear factors
z-m-21-01.s.s3.prompt: Now widen “integer coefficients” to “real coefficients” (two quadratics with x² coefficient 1; order swaps same). Conditions a+c=0, a(d−b)=0, b+d−a²=−5, bd=4 still hold. Which statement best describe number of possible factorizations now?
z-m-21-01.s.s3.hint.0: Start from a(d−b)=0, split a=0 and b=d cases, then write remaining equations for each.
z-m-21-01.s.s3.hint.1: For each case, solve am directly and count how many values b and d fit take as real numbers.
z-m-21-01.s.s3.o.a: Real numbers plenty pass integers, so endless factorisations dey
z-m-21-01.s.s3.r.a: This thinking notice that when allowed numbers increase, answers increase too. But for this case, first think about how the coefficient conditions tie a, b, c, d together?
z-m-21-01.s.s3.o.b: E still be 3. For both cases (when a=0 and when b=d), values don already settle
z-m-21-01.s.s3.r.b: This judgment separate into 2 cases and check whether values don settle for real numbers too.
z-m-21-01.s.s3.o.c: E reduce compared with integers. Real numbers include integers, so condition stricter
z-m-21-01.s.s3.r.c: You reach opposite conclusion from the fact say "real numbers include integers." When allowed range widen, possible factors no fit reduce. Check whether the 3 integer cases still work.
z-m-21-01.s.s3.o.d: Conditions no enough, so we no fit say how many dey
z-m-21-01.s.s3.r.d: This judgment talk say "not enough information" without checking whether the 4 equations enough. Check whether 4 unknowns and 4 equations narrow the values.
z-m-21-01.s.s3.explain: Since a(d−b)=0, a=0 or b=d. If a=0, then b+d=−5 and bd=4, so b and d are only the two roots −1 and −4 of t²+5t+4=0. If b=d, then b²=4 gives b=±2, and a²=2b+5, so when b=2, a=±3, and when b=−2, a=±1. Even for real numbers there is nothing outside these cases, so if we ignore order, still 3 dey. Being integer no filter anything for this case.
